summary: ```# Quick Start Part 2: How to Make a Maid Outfit? (Belt and Shoulder Straps) ## Introduction In this tutorial, we will explore how to create the belt and shoulder straps for a maid outfit using simulation tools. After freezing the tight top coat, we can simulate various versions, while ensuring that the frozen version's shape remains unchanged. ## Creating the Belt Panel 1. **Activate the Sewing Line** The sewing line remains effective even after freezing the top coat. 2. **Using the Rectangular Tool** Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the rectangular tool. Click and drag to create a rectangle approximately three times the width of the virtual model's waist. 3. **Adjusting the Panel Width** Utilize the adjustment panel tool to fine-tune the width as necessary. Press **Ctrl + D** to create a symmetrical panel. 4. **Arranging the Panels** In the 2D window, move the panel and press **Shift + F** to open the arrangement point. Align the two panels at the waist's arrangement points. 5. **Sewing the Panels** Use the line sewing tool in the 2D window. Click on the two lines in the front to complete the sewing line, and then repeat for the back. ## Simulating the Belt 1. **Activating Simulation** After pressing **Ctrl + D** to open the simulation, observe how the panel appears on the virtual model. If the belt is too loose, adjust it manually. 2. **Reactivating Frozen Panels** Reactivate the previously frozen panels, as they are now worn with the belt. Gradually adjust the settings, ensuring the tail-swing rate increases slowly to avoid instability. 3. **Freezing Panels for Stability** Freeze both the completed belt and the top part to maintain their current shapes. This action will enhance software performance during manual adjustments. ## Creating the Shoulder Straps 1. **Positioning the Belt** Move the belt near the waist in the 2D simulation to determine the length of the shoulder straps. 2. **Drawing the Shoulder Strap** Create a rectangular panel for the shoulder strap. Note that since the human body is a three-dimensional model, ensure the strap is drawn long enough. 3. **Copying the Strap Panel** Copy and paste the panel, then press **Ctrl + D** to create a total of four panels—two pairs of shoulder straps. 4. **Arranging the Straps** Press **Shift + F** to open the arrangement point and adjust the position of the x-axis to place the straps closer to the center of the body. ## Sewing the Shoulder Straps 1. **Using 3D or 2D Window** If sewing in the 2D window is inconvenient, switch to the 3D window. Click on a section of the line and then another to sew, ensuring lines do not cross. 2. **Applying Free Sewing** For sewing the entire section of the panel and its smaller section, use free sewing. This technique applies to both the front and back. 3. **Final Adjustments** After simulating the sewing, pause the simulation and assess the shoulder strap's position. Use the **W key** to create a fixed stitch to prevent slipping. ## Refining the Design 1. **Edge Sewing for Better Fit** Use the edge sewing line tool to adjust the sewing line inward on the belt. Check the simulation again to see if the shoulder strap is positioned correctly. 2. **Creating Natural Movement** To make the shoulder strap appear more natural, adjust the length of the line to create a 2 mm space between points. 3. **Adjusting Panel Lengths** If the shoulder strap appears too long, press **Ctrl + Z** to revert to the previous state before the simulation. In the 3D window, switch to hardware image mode (Alt + 7) to analyze stretch. 4. **Identifying Tight Areas** Blue and green areas indicate acceptable stretch, while red areas signify tightness. Adjust the shoulder strap or belt width accordingly. 5. **Synchronizing Adjustments** When adjusting the shoulder strap width, ensure both front and back pieces move simultaneously to maintain symmetry. Hold the **Shift key** to select multiple elements. 6. **Finalizing the Sewing Lines** After adjusting the width, use the editor sewing line tool to equalize the sewing lines, ensuring they match the reference points. ## Conclusion After following these steps, you will have a well-structured belt and shoulder straps for your maid outfit. Remember to regularly simulate and adjust your design to achieve the best results. ```
